p.n: The Cat Calls Back the Rat

body.p:
“Later, the rat tarried wanted to come out of the burrow, but he saw the cat and did not come close to him.
So the cat cried,

p.n: The Cat Reminds the Rat of their Friendship

body.p: ‘Why don’t you approach me, O dear friend

I would love to reward you for your beneficence toward me
and let you taste the fruits of your deed. Approach me and fear not:

for my self is not dearer to me than you,’ and he swore
he did not want to do him harm.”

p.n: The Treatment of Friends or Foes

body.p:
‘He who fails to appease friends and enemies,’ said the rat,
‘harms himself and ruins it.

p.n: One Should Not Befriend an Enemy Indefinitely

body.p:
Enmity and friendship are of such a nature that the wise man should not
fraternize with someone who was an enemy to him, except in the case of necessity.

p.n: Young Cattle Only Nurse for a While

body.p:
The offspring of animals
follow their mothers...

p.n: Enmity Turns into Friendship in Times of Need

body.p:
If a man turns from enmity to friendship for profit,
his amity ends when that profit ends, and he turns to his previous enmity-

as with hot water:
when it is separated from the fire, it reverts to its initial state-coldness.

p.n: The Cat Is the Rat's Worst Enemy

body.p:
You are an enemy unto me,
and I am, likewise, an enemy unto you. How can friendship and amity work between us,

p.n: The Cat Desires the Rat for Food

body.p: while I know that you have no need except that of eating me

p.n: The Last Verdict Is No Reunion

body.p: There is no way for us to reunite.’

“Then the rat went into his burrow
and stood firm in his stance, remaining wary of the cat.”
